---
title: "Documentation"
---

7 requirement(s) in this category.

### DOC-001 — Docstrings on definitions and major theorems {#sec-doc-001}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

Every definition and every major theorem SHALL carry a doc string delimited by `/-- … -/`. Doc strings on lemmas are encouraged, particularly when a lemma has mathematical content or may be reused. A complete-sentence doc string ends in a period.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Each definition has a `/-- … -/` docstring.
- Each major theorem has a docstring.
- `#lint only docBlame docBlameThm` reports no missing docstrings.

**Rationale.** Docstrings are the primary API documentation; the `docBlame` linters enforce their presence.

**Verify.** #lint only docBlame docBlameThm

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html>

---

### DOC-002 — Module docstring after imports {#sec-doc-002}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

Each file SHALL have a module docstring delimited by `/-!` and `-/` (each delimiter on its own line) placed after the imports, containing at least a first-level title and a summary, plus `Main definitions`, `Main statements`, `Notation`, `Implementation notes`, `References`, and `Tags` sections as applicable. `Notation` is required whenever the file introduces notation.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The file has a `/-! … -/` module docstring after the imports.
- It contains a title and a summary.
- Applicable sections (notation, references, tags, …) are present.

**Rationale.** The module docstring is the file's front page for readers and for the generated documentation site.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html>

---

### DOC-003 — Docstrings convey mathematical meaning {#sec-doc-003}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

A doc string SHOULD convey the mathematical meaning of a declaration; it MAY lie slightly about the actual implementation in service of clarity. Named theorems referenced in prose SHOULD be shown in bold.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Docstrings describe the mathematical intent.
- Named theorems appear in bold where referenced.

**Rationale.** Readers want the mathematics, not the encoding; a faithful-in-spirit description beats an implementation dump.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html>

---

### DOC-004 — References via docs/references.bib {#sec-doc-004}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

Bibliographic references SHALL be added to `docs/references.bib` and cited from docstrings as `[key]` or `[custom text][key]`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Cited works exist as entries in `docs/references.bib`.
- Citations use the `[key]` / `[text][key]` forms.

**Rationale.** A single shared bibliography keeps citations consistent and resolvable across the library.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html>

---

### DOC-005 — Markdown and LaTeX conventions in docs {#sec-doc-005}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

In documentation, Lean declarations SHOULD be written in backticks (fully-qualified names become links); raw URLs SHOULD be enclosed in angle brackets `<…>`; inline math uses single `$…$`, display math uses `$$…$$`, and LaTeX environments use `\begin{…}…\end{…}` without dollar signs. Section comments use `/-! … -/` with `###` third-level headers.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Lean names are backticked; URLs are angle-bracketed.
- Math uses `$…$` / `$$…$$`; environments omit dollar signs.

**Rationale.** Uniform markup renders correctly on the documentation site and keeps cross-references live.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html>

---

### DOC-006 — Documentation in English {#sec-doc-006}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHOULD**

Documentation SHOULD be written in English; any common variety (British, American, Australian) is acceptable, though declaration names remain American (see NAM-002).

**Acceptance criteria**

- Prose documentation is in English.

**Rationale.** A shared language keeps documentation usable by the whole community.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html>

---

### DOC-007 — Tags and dependencies on informal results {#sec-doc-007}

**PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

Informal (English-only) definitions and lemmas SHALL carry tags and a dependency list; semi-formal results SHALL carry tags.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Informal results carry tags and a dependency list.
- Semi-formal results carry tags.

**Rationale.** Tags and dependency lists make informal physics content searchable and connect it into the formal dependency graph.

**Source.** <http://physlib.io/getting-started>
